s:
Consider the following statements about human spaceflight:
1. Alan Shepard was the first American in space, while John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth.
2. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, flew on Shenzhou-5 in October 2003.
3. So far only the USSR/Russia, the USA and Japan have launched humans into space on their own.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the three nations with their own crewed launch are USSR/Russia, USA and China; India (Gaganyaan) would be the fourth.

s:
Match List-I (Astronaut) with List-II (Distinction):
List-I (Astronaut) | List-II (Distinction)
a. Rakesh Sharma | i. Indian-origin NASA astronaut on Soyuz MS-29 (2026)
b. Kalpana Chawla | ii. First Indian in space (Soyuz T-11, 1984)
c. Shubhanshu Shukla | iii. First Indian on the ISS
d. Anil Menon | iv. First Indian-origin woman in space (1997)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Rakesh Sharma – Soyuz T-11, Apr 1984; Kalpana Chawla – first Indian-origin woman in space (NASA, 1997); Shubhanshu Shukla – first Indian on the ISS (Axiom-4); Anil Menon – Soyuz MS-29, Jul 2026, eight months.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Axiom-4 mission:
1. It was launched on 25 June 2025 in a SpaceX Dragon on a Falcon 9 rocket.
2. Shubhanshu Shukla stayed about 28 days aboard the ISS.
3. Its crew, commanded by Peggy Whitson, included astronauts from Poland and Hungary.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the crew spent 18 days on the ISS (returned 15 Jul 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan:
1. It was approved in 2018 as India's first human spaceflight programme.
2. It aims to take a crew of three to a low Earth orbit of about 400 km for seven days.
3. The crew module is to splash down in Indian waters and be recovered by the Indian Navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the planned mission lasts 3 days (crew of 3, ~400 km LEO).

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan:
1. It will be launched by the human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) from Sriharikota.
2. The CE-20 engine for the L110 stage of the human-rated LVM3 was qualified in three tests.
3. DRDO provides human-centric systems such as parachutes, life support and crew recovery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the engine of the L110 stage is the Vikas engine, qualified in 3 tests (CE-20 is the cryogenic engine).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Gaganyaan's Orbital Module has only two parts – the Crew Module and the Service Module.
Reason (R): Russia's Soyuz and China's Shenzhou spacecraft each have three modules – orbital, descent and service.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R only contrasts other spacecraft; it does not explain why Gaganyaan has two parts.

s:
Match List-I (Gaganyaan test) with List-II (What it tested):
List-I (Test) | List-II (What it tested)
a. CARE (2014) | i. Crew Escape System abort at Mach 1.2
b. TV-D1 (2023) | ii. 5.7 t module with 10 parachutes of 4 types
c. IADT-01 (2025) | iii. Crew-module re-entry
d. IADT-02 (2026) | iv. 4.8 t module dropped from a Chinook helicopter
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CARE (LVM3-X, 18 Dec 2014) – re-entry; TV-D1 (18 Oct 2023) – crew escape at Mach 1.2; IADT-01 (24 Aug 2025) – 4.8 t from 3 km by IAF Chinook; IADT-02 (10 Apr 2026) – 5.7 t, 10 parachutes.

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan tests:
1. The TV-D1 test flight was conducted at Sriharikota.
2. IADT-01, the first Integrated Air Drop Test, was conducted at SDSC-SHAR.
3. SOLVE (July 2026) was an air-drop test of the crew module parachutes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: SOLVE (3 Jul 2026) was a solid-motor ground test.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyatris named in February 2024:
1. All four are Indian Air Force test pilots.
2. Their selection and aeromedical tests were carried out by the IAF's Institute of Aerospace Medicine, Bengaluru.
3. Their zero-gravity training is given in a centrifuge.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: zero-g training is given through aircraft parabolic flights.

Consider the following statements about the International Space Station:
1. It has been continuously crewed since November 2000.
2. It is expected to retire around 2035.
3. Its module Kibo was contributed by Japan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the ISS is expected to retire around 2030.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS):
1. The full station is to be completed by 2040.
2. It was approved in September 2024 and will have five modules.
3. Its base module BAS-1 is targeted for 2028 on the LVM3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the full BAS is targeted for 2035; 2040 is the target for an Indian on the Moon.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The mass of an astronaut in an orbiting satellite becomes zero.
Reason (R): In an orbiting satellite the craft and the astronaut fall with the same acceleration, so the normal force on the astronaut is zero.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: in weightlessness the weight (felt as normal force) becomes zero but the mass stays the same. R is true: free fall with the same g makes the normal force zero.

Match List-I (Condition in microgravity) with List-II (Effect):
List-I (Condition) | List-II (Effect)
a. Bone loss | i. Space motion sickness
b. Fluid shift | ii. Weakening of postural muscles
c. Space Adaptation Syndrome | iii. 1–1.5% of bone mass a month
d. Muscle atrophy | iv. 'Puffy face, bird legs'
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Bone loss – 1–1.5% a month; fluid shift – puffy face, bird legs (Charlie Brown effect); Space Adaptation Syndrome – space motion sickness; muscle atrophy – postural muscles weaken.

Match List-I (Facility) with List-II (Role / feature):
List-I (Facility) | List-II (Role)
a. Human Space Flight Centre, Bengaluru | i. Tracking network
b. ISTRAC, Bengaluru | ii. New ISRO vertical leading Gaganyaan
c. Dhanush, Sriharikota | iii. SSLV launch complex
d. Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu | iv. India's first private launch pad (Agnikul Cosmos)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: HSFC – new ISRO vertical for Gaganyaan; ISTRAC – tracking network; Dhanush – Agnikul Cosmos' private pad; Kulasekarapattinam – SSLV complex (foundation 27 Aug 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota:
1. The Union Cabinet approved it in January 2025.
2. It will cost about Rs 10,000 crore.
3. It is meant for the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) and human spaceflight.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the approved cost is about Rs 4,000 crore.

Consider the following statements about analogue missions in Ladakh:
1. India's first analogue space mission at Leh (November 2024) was conducted by ISRO with AAKA and IIT Madras.
2. The HOPE habitat at Tso Kar was chosen because its conditions resemble early Mars – high UV, low pressure and cold.
3. MITRA was a crew behavioural study at Leh with the IAF's Institute of Aerospace Medicine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the partner institute was IIT Bombay.
